title: IREN Stock: Buy or Sell?
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Parkevtate explains why IREN is down 68% over six months and whether the dip is a buying opportunity. The latest quarter had good news: new multi-year contracts, including with a leading frontier AI lab, took the revenue backlog above $20 billion, two-thirds of it with investment-grade customers; Horizon 1 was handed over to Microsoft with Nvidia exemplar cloud status; operating annual recurring revenue doubled to $1 billion and adjusted EBITDA margin rose from 14% to 29%. The bad news is execution: the target of more than $4 billion of operating ARR online by the end of 2026 has slipped to January or February 2027 while remaining equipment arrives, which he reads as a warning about delivering on contracted timelines amid industry-wide supply shortages. Demand itself has not slowed: contracts signed at $22 million of annualised revenue per megawatt on five-year terms, and over $40 million per megawatt on shorter terms, with customer prepayments covering about 90% of the associated GPU capex. The balance sheet is worsening, with $10.2 billion of long-term debt against $5.7 billion of cash, versus roughly $7 billion of each a few months ago. He argues IREN differs from a typical neocloud because it owns the land, power, infrastructure and compute, giving lenders collateral. Forward price-to-sales is about 1, the cheapest since 2024, and his updated DCF fair value is $32 against a $19.73 market price. Call: IREN BUY reiterated, medium conviction: one of the riskiest stocks in the market, but the reward justifies the risk.

calls.thesis: BUY reiterated, medium conviction — one of the riskiest stocks in the market, but reward justifies the risk; $20bn+ backlog, cheapest on forward price-to-sales since 2024.
calls.base_case: Backlog converts to revenue; $4bn ARR target slips only to Jan/Feb 2027 on equipment delays.
calls.bull_case: Demand unslowed, $22m/MW 5-year contracts with ~90% customer prepay of GPU capex.
calls.bear_case: Execution slips and heavy upfront capex strain the balance sheet ($10.2bn debt vs $5.7bn cash).
